questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I liked the fact that Bologna was a studycity, a smaller city and close to many other interesting italian cities which I could visit during my exchange. 
I also looked for a destination which had exciting culture and a great study-environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved being on exchange in Bologna

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy by using UniBo's website, to find signup for check-in etc. UniBo has a guide for incoming exchangestudents, although it is a bit outdated, but still helpfull.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did a check-in online, but basically the direct contact with unibo was non-excistent, so no actual help as such, I was just informed that my check in went through.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I didn't need a lot of information, so it didnt bother me, that there wasnt a lot to be found. There were emails to contact if anyone had additional troubles.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very hard. Bologna has a lot of issues with housing for both exchange students, permanent students and normal residents. Search in advance and don't expect to find something right away. Be aware of scammers on facebook. It is also expensive, especially if you want to be in the center of the city.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Bologna is a small city, it is great. There's different campus throughout the city, so it depends on the courses you take how far you have, but generally the city is small so it is all doable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You don't have to sign up for courses in advance, you just show up on the classes and you therefore have some time to figure out if the courses you like are actually interesting. The professors will tell you how to officially sign up, but you don't have to do it before going to the first class.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Talk to the professors responsible for the course you're interested in if you have any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was pretty good, just hard to make the puzzle work and combine all the courses I was interested in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to your professors, they only want to help!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took MA courses, but the level was not that advanced anyways.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More seminar-like than lecture-like often. The professors will ask you direct questions on the reading, and being active in the courses is often a requirement.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Web Society and Globalization, Urban Studies and Climate Change, Humanitarian Communication, Visualizing the Italian Society.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Humanitarian Communication, as the professor is very engaged in his teaching material and in general very interesting. The Visualizing the Italian society course was also great, it was a discussion of older Italian Cinema, and the professor was a cool guy. The exam in this course was also pretty easy, so it's a good and interesting course with easy workload.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None really, any books needed for the courses were available online which was nice and easy.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: You will spend more money on drinks and food than you except - even though it's cheaper, you will just end up buying more and eating out more, which is really nice to do and indulge in, but it ends up being expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were really none easy to be able to join, the sports clubs had a mandatory doctor-checkup to be able to join, which was a bit complicated to do in the city.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports and some academic presentations and workshops.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't really engage in many of them, the academic activities were mostly in italian.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the cities outside of Bologna, It is a perfect opportunity for daytrips to venice, florence, ravenna etc. Walk around the city and find the good cafe's. It's a great city to be in, so enjoy and live the sweet italian life.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, it came naturally as the culture is still close to danish culture. Just take it slow and enjoy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Most of the people you will naturally meet are exchange students like you, but maybe you  live with italian people who can help you get in touch with local people if you want to.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think the only thing is, that a lot of italians could be uncomfortable with their english, even though most spoke it perfectly fine.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love the coffee-culture and sitting down for just an espresso at a cute cafe. People are very open and will talk to you if you let them. The culture is very open and warm, people are kind.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Time goes fast, so enjoy. If you live outside the city center, find a bike and a very good lock for it. Coffee and drinks are cheap, so remember to take advantage of that. Be open and talk to people and dont be scared.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Italian system is so much slower and less structured than what we're used to at KU - don't worry, It will all work out.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience of being away from normal life and trying a completely new every-day life. The people I met and had fun with, and all the personal evolvement when doing something which is a bit outside your comfort zone.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Mostly just that it was over way to quickly.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
